title: Canonical localization presentation data
statement: For a prime \(\ell\), a finite extension \(E/\mathbf Q_\ell\), and a scheme \(X\), use the completed integral coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For a morphism \(i:Z\to X\), retain the specified coefficient comparison, module inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, its unit \(\eta\), its kernel, and the kernel inclusion. A presentation in any category \(\mathcal C\) is two endofunctors \(F,H\) with maps \(F\to\mathrm{id}\to H\). Retain unchanged the finite, integral, rational, common-stage and Weil normalization and conclusion predicates of the parent proposition. When \(i\) is a closed immersion and \(X\) is Noetherian, closed direct image preserves finite limits and colimits, the specified counit is invertible, the specified unit is epic at every module, and its actual kernel sequence is pointwise short exact.

proof.text: Transport the ringed closed adjunction through the specified coefficient equivalence. Uniqueness of adjoints conjugates its unit by an isomorphism, so its components remain epic. The counit is invertible by full faithfulness. The kernel sequence is exact and evaluation preserves it.

theorem sfRecollementModule_shortExact {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsNoetherian X]
    (M : scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X) :
    (ShortComplex.mk ((sfRecollementModuleCounit l E i).app M)
      ((sfRecollementModuleUnit l E i).app M)
      (by exact congr_app (kernel.condition (sfRecollementModuleUnit l E i)) M)).ShortExact
